successors.name: Electorate of Brandenburg
successors.text: the Mark Brandenburg under the Hohenzollern, with the Altmark, without the pawned Neumark and the Międzyrzecz castellany; 'On 20 March 1414, the Brandenburg estates swore allegiance at Tangermünde'…

ledger.x: 1260: the Ascanian Margraviate of Brandenburg enters the map.
1261: the Ascanians buy Soldin.
1262: the Ascanian margraves hold Upper Lusatia.

1272: Cliopatria's outline adds the Neumark east of the Oder: 35 of them lie inside its Duchy of Greater Poland shape of 1271, 17 inside its Holy Roman Empire Minor States shape, one in neither; this event…
1272: the other 17 cells of the Neumark step, in the north.
1296: Brandenburg annexes Deutsch Krone.
1297: Brandenburg annexes the Międzyrzecz castellany from Greater Poland.
1303: the Ascanian margraves acquire Lower Lusatia from the Wettins.
1307: Waldemar takes Pomerelia in hand.
1309-09-13: by the Treaty of Soldin Brandenburg gives up Pomerelia to the Teutonic Order.
1316: Waldemar occupies Dresden again.
1317: the feud with Meissen ends and Dresden is no longer occupied.
1317: Waldemar surrenders Stargard and Neubrandenburg.
1317: Waldemar waives Schlawe and Stolp.
1319: Waldemar acquires Züllichau and Schwiebus.
1319: the south of Lower Lusatia goes to the Duchy of Jawor.
1319: northern Lower Lusatia leaves Brandenburg's hands.
1319: the Bohemian king takes western Upper Lusatia.
1319: eastern Upper Lusatia passes to the Duchy of Jawor.
1319: Wartislaw IV of Pomerania takes the New March.
1320: a large portion of the Lubusz Land passes to Henry I of Jawor.
1322: Henry IV of Żagań holds the Międzyrzecz castellany.
1323: Emperor Louis IV gives Brandenburg to his son Louis I; the Wittelsbach era begins.
1324: northern Lower Lusatia passes to the Wittelsbach margraves.
1326: the New March is bridged back to Brandenburg.
1326: the Torzym-Sulęcin cells are bridged back.
1356: the Golden Bull makes Brandenburg an electorate.
1367: Otto V sells Lower Lusatia to Charles IV.
1368: Casimir the Great takes Deutsch Krone.
1373: Charles IV buys Brandenburg for 500,000 guilders and the Luxembourg era begins.
1402: the Luxembourgs pawn the Neumark to the Teutonic Order.
1411: Frederick of Nuremberg, a Hohenzollern, is granted hereditary control of Brandenburg.
1414: the estates swear allegiance to Frederick of Hohenzollern at Tangermünde, 20 March 1414; the state goes on as the Electorate of Brandenburg.

wars.name: Waldemar's Pomerelian venture and the Treaty of Soldin
wars.outcome: 'In 1307 Waldemar signed an agreement with the Swienca family ceding him the lands of Pomerelia'; Brandenburg troops held strategic places 'up to Gdańsk'; by the 1309 Treaty of Soldin he 'relinquished his claims on Pomerelia east of the Łeba River to the…

wars.name: Brandenburg-Meissen feud over Lusatia and Dresden
wars.outcome: 1312: Frederick of Meissen cedes 'the March of Lusatia as well as the towns of Torgau and Großenhain'; 1316: Waldemar 'again occupied Dresden until the feud with Meissen was finally brought to an end in 1317'.

wars.name: Waldemar's war with Mecklenburg and Pomerania (Gransee 1316, Treaty of Templin 1317)
wars.outcome: 'In August 1316, Waldemar's troops were defeated near Gransee'; by the 1317 Treaty of Templin 'the margrave had to surrender Stargard and Neubrandenburg to Mecklenburg' and waive Schlawe and Stolp, which passed to Duke Wartislaw IV of Pomerania.

wars.name: Brandenburg succession conflict after the Ascanian extinction
wars.outcome: After the extinction of the Ascanian line neighbours seized the margraviate piecemeal: Pomerania the New March (1319), Jawor and then Żagań the Lubusz Land (1320-1322), Saxe-Wittenberg the north of Lower Lusatia and parts of the Uckermark; Pomerania and…

wars.name: Polish invasion of Frankfurt (Oder)
wars.outcome: 'In 1326, Polish King Władysław I invaded Frankfurt (Oder).'

certainty.note: No page opened gives a survey or treaty line for the Mark; the Oder-side frontier, the Neumark and the Lusatian edge are Cliopatria's approximations, and the lump-and-correct work of 1326-1384 rests on its outlines.
